### 1.1 Pretrained Models with Hugging Face · T1
**Idea:** A released model is a configuration file plus tensors, and its memory and speed follow from the configuration.
**Opening:** The reader has `d2l.GPT` and its GPT-2 weights. Three lines load Qwen3.5-2B and it answers a question the book's model cannot. The section reads the repository until every field of the configuration maps to a section of this book and to a number of bytes, and it closes on the question of whether those same tensors would run in the book's own code.
**Teaches:**
- Repository anatomy: the model card, `config.json`, sharded safetensors with their index, the tokenizer files, `generation_config.json`; a revision is a commit hash, and a pinned load passes it to both model and tokenizer.
- The Auto classes, `dtype` and `device_map`, `generate` and its sampling fields mapped onto the sampler of `sec_decoding`; one chat template serves base, instruct and thinking variants, and the rendered token sequence is printed so the text cannot drift from the file.
- Qwen3.5's configuration read field by field: Gated DeltaNet layers with one full-attention layer in four (`sec_deltanet`, `sec_hybrids`, read as fields only), gated attention and partial RoPE, a multi-token-prediction head, a vision tower; Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.8 are the same architecture at larger scale, said in one sentence.
- Gemma 4 E2B as the second family: per-layer embeddings, sliding windows interleaved with global layers, text-only loading; the same derivation applied to a different configuration.
- Pinning, licences and `trust_remote_code` in two sentences with a link to `sec_software_ecosystem`.
**Derivation:** Bytes to run a model from its configuration: weights (parameters times bytes per element, counted by group so the sum reconciles to the safetensors header), KV cache per token for full-attention layers (2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × bytes), the fixed recurrent state of linear-attention layers (independent of context), the activation workspace of one forward pass and the logits term. Smallest numeric case: one full-attention layer with 2 KV heads of head dimension 256 in bf16 caches 2 × 2 × 256 × 2 = 2,048 bytes per token; a hybrid with one such layer in four and a 19.5 MB fixed state crosses an all-attention stack of the same width at a context the reader solves for.
**Notebook:**
1. Load Qwen3.5-2B pinned to its commit with `d2l.load_hf`; read the safetensors header by HTTP range request without downloading tensors (`d2l.safetensors_header`); reconcile the header's element count to `d2l.config_params(by_group=True)` (language model, vision tower, MTP head) exactly.
2. Derive the memory terms with `d2l.config_memory`; prefill contexts of 256, 1,024, 4,096 and 16,384 tokens from a committed passage and compare the cache walker's bytes and the allocator's growth with the formula.
3. Time 64 greedy decode steps at each context with `d2l.Benchmark` (3 warm-ups, 10 repeats, median and interquartile band) and plot tokens per second against the bandwidth ceiling of `eq_hw_decode_bound` with the card's datasheet bandwidth.
4. Repeat steps 1 to 3 for Gemma 4 E2B (text-only); the per-layer embedding tables enter the weight term, the sliding layers cache at most the window.
5. Claim that survives noise: measured memory is within 10% of the derived total at every context for both models (the allocator's block rounding is the gap); measured decode speed is within a factor of 2 of the bandwidth ceiling, with the gap's size stated as measured and the launch overhead counted with the profiler in one decode step.
6. Reused pieces: `d2l.Benchmark`, `d2l.sample_next` as the semantic reference for Transformers' sampling arguments; the KV byte formula `eq_kv-cache-bytes` recapped in one paragraph.
**Figures:** `fig_lm_hub_repo` (what a repository holds and which file each loader reads); `fig_lm_memory_vs_config` (plot: cache bytes and decode tokens per second against context for both models, formula lines and the all-attention counterfactual).
**Restate / forward:** `subsec_hw-two-workloads` (decode reads every weight once per token, so its speed is a bandwidth ratio); `eq_kv-cache-bytes` (the KV cache grows linearly in context); `sec_software_ecosystem` (pinned revisions, licences, why `trust_remote_code` is off). Forward: 14.1 reads whole families this way.
**Exercises:** 6 to 8. Load-bearing: derive Gemma 4 E2B's KV bytes per token from its configuration and the context at which its cache equals the per-layer embedding tables (derive); measure decode tokens per second against batch size 1 to 32 and locate the batched-decode crossover (measure); check the parameter count of Qwen3-0.6B's post-trained file against its base file and explain the duplicate head (check); open: at what context length does a hybrid's cache plus state equal an all-attention stack's, and what does that say about long-context serving.
**Writer notes:**
- Library exports with fixed signatures (`01_interfaces.md`): `d2l.load_hf(model_id, revision=None, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map='auto') -> (model, tokenizer)` always passes `revision` to both objects, sets `trust_remote_code=False`, `use_safetensors=True`, warns if `hf_device_map` spreads modules over devices (silent CPU offload is the performance trap); `d2l.config_params(config, include_vision=False, include_mtp=False, by_group=False)` raises `NotImplementedError('use d2l.config_stats (14.1)')` on MoE configs; `d2l.config_memory(config, seq_len, batch_size, dtype_bytes=2, *, state_bytes=4, ...)` returns the keys `params, weights, kv_cache, recurrent_state, activations, logits, total` and reads `layer_types` (`full_attention`, `sliding_attention` with `sliding_window`, `linear_attention`); `d2l.HF_REVISIONS` loads `data/lm_revisions.json`.
- Gemma 4 adds two configuration shapes `config_memory` must handle before authoring: per-layer embedding tables (weights, not activations) and sliding layers; the blueprint's `config_memory` was written for Qwen3.5 only, so extend it and add a test per model. Numbers on the Gemma 4 cards are secondary in `sota.md`; read sizes and windows off the card at authoring.
- Silent breakages: `generation_config.json` may set sampling (Qwen3.5-2B has none, so defaults are greedy); the state dtype of the live cache (the config's `mamba_ssm_dtype` is float32) must be read off the cache, not assumed; `torch_dtype` versus `dtype` across Transformers versions; `model.parameters()` deduplicates tied weights and `state_dict()` does not; the MTP weights are loaded but unused by `generate` (12.5 uses them).
- Transformers version drift: Qwen3.5 modeling code is recent (`transformers >= 5.2`); the cache-walker cell is written against `cache.get_recurrent_state` and `get_conv_state` with a generic fallback that sums every tensor found by traversal. Print the bound kernel (`chunk_gated_delta_rule` fast versus the torch fallback) and run either way.
- Do not re-teach: BPE (`sec_text-sequence`; print the two vocabularies' sizes and tokens per character only), the sampler (`sec_decoding`), safetensors as a format (`sec_read_write`), the decode bound (`sec_hardware`), the DeltaNet recurrence (`chap_modern_rnn`). The section makes the one forward reference to 14.1 and no field-by-field forward references.
- Anecdotes stay anecdotes: prompts compared across thinking modes are labelled as such; no accuracy claim from them.
- Committed artifacts: `data/lm_revisions.json`; the Qwen3.5-2B header (`lm-qwen35-2b-header.json`, about 100 KB) so the reconciliation runs offline; the measured table behind the figure.
- Confirm at authoring the exact Gemma 4 E2B id to pin (`google/gemma-4-E2B` or `-it`; the instruct variant serves the chat comparison).
**Sources:**
- Papers: [Transformers: State-of-the-Art Natural Language Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.03771) (the library's design); [Qwen3 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388) (Table 1 for the dense architectures that 1.2 ports; the thinking switch).
- Code and documentation: [Transformers documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/index) and its [quick tour](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/quicktour); [generation strategies](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/generation_strategies) (the sampling fields mapped onto `sec_decoding`); [model cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards); [safetensors](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors/index) (header format, read by range request); [PyTorch profiler recipe](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/recipes/recipes/profiler_recipe.html) (counting launches in one decode step); model cards [Qwen3.5-2B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B), [Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B), [Qwen3.5-0.8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B), [Gemma 4 E2B](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it) (sizes, windows, per-layer embeddings: read at authoring); [Qwen3.8 README](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.8) (the larger models of the same architecture).
- Courses, tutorials and blogs: [Hugging Face LLM Course, chapter 2](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter2/1) (the Auto-class tour); [CS336](https://cs336.stanford.edu/) (resource accounting lecture: FLOPs, memory, arithmetic intensity).

### 1.2 A Released Checkpoint in the Book's Own Code · T1
**Idea:** The same tensors run in a subclass of `d2l.GPT` and match the reference layer by layer.
**Opening:** Qwen3-0.6B's first block almost fits the constructor the reader already has: grouped-query attention, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE. The three differences (an explicit head dimension wider than the residual, QK-norm, a RoPE base of one million) are a small diff. The section writes the diff, maps the weights, and closes on what a layer-by-layer match exposes that a final-logit check hides.
**Teaches:**
- The three subclasses `d2l.Qwen3Attention(GQAAttention)` (explicit `head_dim`, `qk_norm`, `rope_theta`, a cached `forward_step`), `d2l.SwiGLU(FeedForward)` (explicit width) and `d2l.Qwen3GPT(GPT)` (assembled through the `attn_factory` and `ffn_factory` hooks of `sec_transformer-block`; untied head for 8B), built on the meta device and loaded with `assign=True`; the book's classes are unchanged (blueprint README Decision 4).
- The weight map as strict accounting: every Hugging Face tensor consumed, every target key produced; the RoPE layout as the silent breakage (Transformers stores the two halves, the book interleaves; the permutation also applies to `q_norm` and `k_norm`), fused versus separate projections, the duplicated `lm_head` in post-trained files.
- Localizing a mismatch: relative error per layer and sublayer against hooks on the reference, and the rule that a divergence is a layer whose error exceeds ten times the clean port's error at that layer.
- `d2l.generate` as the part's batched sampler over any model that returns logits, with `d2l.Generation` records and the cached path through `forward_cached`.
- Why the book reimplements Qwen3 and not Qwen3.5: the hybrid layers need `chap_modern_rnn`'s code, which 14.6 adds.
**Derivation:** none.
**Notebook:**
1. Build `d2l.Qwen3GPT` from the configuration through `d2l.qwen3_gpt_kwargs` and load Qwen3-0.6B with `d2l.load_qwen3`; assert the parameter count equals the shape-based count of 1.1.
2. Capture `attn_out`, `resid_mid`, `mlp_out`, `resid_post` per layer from the port and from Transformers (eager attention, TF32 off) on 32 committed prompts of 64 tokens; plot relative error per layer in fp32 and bf16 against the reference's own bf16-versus-fp32 floor.
3. Inject five porting bugs (missing RoPE permutation, wrong theta, swapped gate and up projections, missing QK-norm, wrong epsilon) and show where `d2l.first_divergence` localizes each; the epsilon bug is the one a final-logit check misses.
4. Greedy-decode 64 tokens on the 32 prompts with `d2l.generate` on the port and with Transformers; report the first index of divergence per prompt.
5. Claim that survives noise: fp32 logits agree within a stated absolute tolerance (provisional 1e-3, replaced by three times the reference's measured CPU-versus-GPU difference if larger); bf16 mean absolute logit error of the port is at most 1.5 times the reference's own bf16 error; greedy tokens are identical for 64 steps on all but near-tie prompts, counted. The computation is deterministic with TF32 off: run twice and assert bitwise-equal captures.
6. Reused pieces: `d2l.GQAAttention`, `d2l.FeedForward`, `d2l.TransformerBlock`, `d2l.GPT.generate` (unchanged), the saved `generate_cached`; the GPT-2 loading cell of `subsec_gpt-loading` recapped in one paragraph.
**Figures:** `fig_lm_weight_map` (Hugging Face names and layouts on the left, `d2l.Qwen3GPT` module names on the right, the RoPE permutation drawn on one head); `fig_lm_layer_divergence` (plot: relative error per layer for the clean port in fp32 and bf16 and for the five bugs).
**Restate / forward:** `subsec_gpt-loading` (GPT-2 weights were mapped by name and shape and checked by loss and greedy tokens; this is the second instance); `sec_transformer-block` (QK-norm normalizes queries and keys per head before RoPE); `sec_positional-information` (RoPE rotates pairs of coordinates; only the pairing convention differs here).
**Exercises:** 5 to 7. Load-bearing: derive the parameter count of Qwen3-8B from its safetensors index and explain which tensors the tied 0.6B file lacks (derive); measure the drift of a port with the wrong RoPE layout as a function of position (measure); check that `d2l.generate` on the port and the Transformers model agree under top-p sampling with a shared seed, and say why batch composition can break the agreement (check).
**Writer notes:**
- The exported names and module layout are relied on by Chapters 4, 6, 11, 12, 13 and 14 and must be exactly: `model.token_emb`; `model.blks[i].attention.{W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o, q_norm, k_norm}` with attributes `head_dim, num_heads, num_kv_heads, rope_theta`; `model.blks[i].ffn.{W_g, W_1, W_2}` computing `W_2(silu(W_g x) * W_1 x)`; `model.norm`; `model.lm_head` only when untied. There are no `W_gate/W_up/W_down`. `isinstance(model, d2l.GPT)` holds.
- The subclasses skip their parents' `__init__` to avoid allocating default-width layers (gigabytes at 8B) and therefore depend on the parents' attribute names (`act`, `pos`, `max_len`, `blks`, `token_emb`, `norm`); the GPT-to-`Qwen3GPT` equivalence test exists to catch a book-side rename.
- `d2l.generate(model, tokenizer, prompts, max_new_tokens=None, *, strategy='greedy', temperature=1.0, k=None, p=None, min_p=None, seed=0, eos_token_ids=None, stop=None, chat=False, enable_thinking=None, return_logprobs=False, batch_size=8) -> list[d2l.Generation]` accepts a `d2l.GPT` (cached path), a Transformers model (own loop with `past_key_values` and left padding) or any module with `model(input_ids) -> logits`; `d2l.GPT` batches only equal-length prompts (no attention mask), so it buckets by length. Qwen3's tokenizer adds no BOS; adding one shifts every logit. Post-trained Qwen3 stops on `<|im_end|>` and `<|endoftext|>`.
- The book marks `sec_kv-cache`'s `generate_cached` cell `#@save` (the blueprint README lists it as optional; this plan requires it), so `Qwen3GPT` overrides `forward` and `forward_cached` and inherits `generate` and `generate_cached`. If the edit has not landed when authoring starts, keep the blueprint's 12-line override and delete it afterwards.
- Reference and tolerance: Transformers with `attn_implementation='eager'` for the layer match (SDPA changes rounding); fp32 with TF32 off; hooks rather than `output_hidden_states` (its last entry may be post-norm in some versions); PyTorch's `nn.RMSNorm` epsilon default depends on dtype, so pass it explicitly.
- Memory: two fp32 copies of 0.6B are about 5 GB; 4B loads in bf16 (8 GB) for a logits check; 8B (16.4 GB) exceeds a 15 GiB slot, so the build exercises it by header and mapping dry run only, and an optional cell guarded by `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` loads it where a larger card exists (the only real-weights test of `tie_embeddings=False`).
- Do not re-teach: name mapping and parameter reconstruction in general (`subsec_gpt-loading`); RoPE; the KV cache arithmetic.
- Committed artifacts: `qwen3_0.6b_logit_reference.pt` (fp32 reference logits on the 32 prompts, stored as top-100 per position plus full last-position logits, about 2 MB); the layer-error table as CSV; the three hidden corrupted state dicts for A1 live outside the notebook.
- `d2l.qwen3_gpt_kwargs` raises on `use_sliding_window`, `rope_scaling` or `attention_bias`; confirm at authoring that no Qwen3 dense checkpoint in the ladder sets them.
**Sources:**
- Papers: [Qwen3 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388) (architecture paragraph: GQA, RoPE base, QK-norm replacing the QKV bias).
- Code and documentation: [Qwen3-0.6B model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B) (configuration, generation defaults, licence); [safetensors documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors/index); [`modeling_qwen3.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/qwen3/modeling_qwen3.py) (the reference being matched; the oracle for the RoPE layout); [PyTorch serialization notes](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/serialization.html) (`load_state_dict(assign=True)` on meta-device modules).
- Courses, tutorials and blogs: Sebastian Raschka, [LLMs from Scratch](https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch) and his [from-scratch materials](https://www.sebastianraschka.com/from-scratch/) (the closest sibling: the same checkpoint and the same permutation question); [Hugging Face LLM Course, chapter 2](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter2/1) (the Auto-class machinery the port bypasses).

### 1.3 Prompting and In-Context Learning · T1
**Idea:** The prompt is tokens, and few-shot accuracy depends on how the demonstrations are laid out.
**Opening:** The reader asks a base checkpoint to classify a news headline and gets a continuation instead of a label. Four solved examples placed before the query lift accuracy by tens of points, and the rendered template shows why: the model continues a pattern of tokens. The section measures what in that pattern matters and closes on what a few-shot score therefore measures.
**Teaches:**
- A chat template as token ids: roles, special tokens, the generation prefix and the thinking switch, printed as the rendered tail so the text cannot drift from the template file; `d2l.fewshot_prompt` renders plain, question-answer and chat layouts.
- Zero- and few-shot formats; scoring by restricted next-token logits over the label words (`d2l.label_logprobs`), the special case that 1.4 generalizes.
- Sensitivity to the number, order and label correctness of demonstrations, with contextual calibration as the one correction worked (`d2l.calibrate_labels`).
- In-context learning against a weight update: the same labelled examples as a probe on frozen features, at equal labelled data and unequal cost.
**Derivation:** none.
**Notebook:**
1. Render the chat template of Qwen3-1.7B for one conversation and print the token ids with the special tokens marked; render the same demonstrations as plain text for the base checkpoint.
2. On 200 stratified test items of a four-class news task, measure accuracy of Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-1.7B against the number of demonstrations (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16) with 3 demonstration seeds.
3. At 8 demonstrations, measure accuracy over four orders of the same demonstrations per seed; then over a fraction of deliberately wrong labels (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) with natural and with abstract label words.
4. Fit a logistic probe on the frozen base model's mean-pooled features with the same labelled examples and add it to the plot.
5. Claim that survives noise: order alone moves accuracy by several points (the spread over orders is comparable to the spread over demonstration sets); shuffled labels cost less than removing the demonstrations altogether for natural label words. Each claim needs a paired bootstrap interval over items that excludes zero and an effect larger than the across-seed standard deviation; 200 items give about plus or minus 7 points unpaired, so the text interprets only paired differences.
6. Reused pieces: `d2l.load_hf`, `d2l.generate` for free-generation spot checks, a 6-line local bootstrap (the shared `d2l.paired_bootstrap` arrives in 1.5 and the text says so).
**Figures:** `fig_lm_chat_template` (the rendered conversation as a token sequence with roles, special tokens and the generation prefix labelled); `fig_lm_icl_sensitivity` (plot: accuracy against demonstration count for base, instruct and the probe; a strip plot of accuracy over orders at k = 8).
**Restate / forward:** `sec_what-attention-computes` (an induction head copies what followed an earlier occurrence of the current token; the repeated-sequence probe is the behavioural signature of in-context copying, and `tab_induction-evidence` says what a behavioural result can claim). Forward: 1.4 (what a restricted-logit score does not measure).
**Exercises:** 5 to 7. Load-bearing: measure the spread of accuracy over 20 orders of the same 8 demonstrations and compare it with the spread over 20 demonstration sets (measure); derive why subtracting the content-free log-probabilities shifts the model's label prior and when it cannot help (derive); open: design a prompt format whose few-shot accuracy for the base model is within the order spread of the instruct model's, and report the cost per query of each.
**Writer notes:**
- Exports: `d2l.fewshot_prompt(demos, query, template='plain', *, label_map=None, system=None)` returning a string or a message list; `d2l.label_logprobs(model, tokenizer, prompts, label_words, *, batch_size=8, chat=False, enable_thinking=False)` returning log-probabilities renormalized over the label set, which asserts the label words' first tokens are distinct and single after the format's separator (the leading-space convention: encode `separator + word` and take the last token of the difference); `d2l.calibrate_labels(logprobs, content_free_logprobs)`.
- Silent breakages: leading-space tokenization of label words (`" Sports"` versus `"Sports"`) when a format changes; chat-templating a base model or omitting the template for an instruct model and attributing the change to ability; Qwen3 post-trained defaults to thinking on and Qwen3.5 to off, read from the pinned template file; test items or near-duplicates leaking into the demonstration pool.
- Data: `fancyzhx/ag_news` (train 120,000 for demonstrations, test 7,600; licence listed as unknown on the Hub, so the notebook downloads it at run time and commits only item indices and predictions); the fallback with a clear licence is ARC-style multiple choice (`allenai/ai2_arc`, CC BY-SA 4.0), with the same code.
- The notebook reduces the blueprint's grid: four orders instead of twelve (twenty orders is the exercise), three seeds, 200 items; the committed per-item grid `lm-fewshot-grid.csv` makes the figure cells seconds at T0.
- What a few-shot score measures: with natural labels much of the gain is format and label-space information rather than the input-label mapping (Min et al.); the section says this and does not call it "learning the task". Restricted-logit accuracy is not free-generation accuracy; 1.4 owns that distinction.
- Cost: few-shot is not free; the probe comparison is at equal labelled data, not equal cost, and the text says which.
- Do not re-teach the induction circuit; restate it in two sentences with the label.
- Decide at authoring, with the editor, whether the clearly licensed ARC fallback is the default task.
**Sources:**
- Papers: [Language Models are Few-Shot Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165) (few-shot as a capability of scale); [Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.12837) (label correctness matters less than format and label space); [In-context Learning and Induction Heads](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.11895) (the mechanistic account restated from `sec_what-attention-computes`); [Calibrate Before Use](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09690) (contextual calibration); [Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08786) (order sensitivity).
- Code and documentation: Transformers, [chat templating](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/chat_templating) (the rendered template and `add_generation_prompt`); [lm-evaluation-harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) (its few-shot construction options as the oracle).
- Courses, tutorials and blogs: [CS224N](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs224n/) (prompting and efficient adaptation lecture); [Hugging Face LLM Course, chapter 2](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter2/1) (tokenizers and templates).

### 1.4 Scoring Language Models · T1
**Idea:** A score is a convention, and two conventions can rank two models differently.
**Opening:** One multiple-choice item scored by the log-probability of each answer's text, by the log-probability of its letter, and by a generated answer gives three verdicts for the same model. The section makes each convention explicit, builds the scorers every later chapter imports, and closes on how many items it takes before a difference means anything.
**Teaches:**
- Log-likelihood scoring: the cloze format against the letter format, length normalization by token, character and byte (`d2l.score_choices` with `norm` in `sum`, `token`, `char`, `byte`, one forward pass yielding every convention through `d2l.ScoreComponents`), and the harness's continuation-splitting convention.
- Generative answers and extraction (`d2l.extract_answer` for GSM8K-style and boxed answers), execution checks (`d2l.run_python_tests`, not a security boundary), and why scoring only the answer option mischaracterizes a model meant to reason before answering.
- pass@k from a common sample pool (`d2l.pass_at_k`); majority voting as a different selection policy.
- Bits per byte as the tokenizer-free likelihood score (`d2l.bits_per_byte` with sliding windows); chrF and BLEU restated in one sentence as string-overlap conventions for generated text.
- Determinism controls: batch-dependent kernels change bf16 near-ties, so the batch size is part of the protocol and the disagreement rate between batch sizes 1 and 8 is reported beside every flip table.
**Derivation:** The unbiased pass@k estimator from n samples with c correct, 1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k), its product form for stable evaluation, and its variance when each sample succeeds independently with probability p. Smallest numeric case: n = 4, c = 1, k = 2 gives 1 - C(3, 2) / C(4, 2) = 1 - 3/6 = 0.5, against the biased 1 - (1 - 1/4)^2 = 0.4375.
**Notebook:**
1. Score Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B on 500 seeded ARC-Challenge items under cloze-sum, cloze-token, cloze-char and letter conventions from one forward pass per format; compare `d2l.score_choices` against committed lm-evaluation-harness per-item choices on 200 items (at most 2 of 200 differ per norm).
2. Score the same items generatively: free generation, `d2l.extract_answer`, exact match; add 100 GSM8K problems with an 8-sample pool for pass@k at k = 1, 2, 4, 8 and compare with majority voting.
3. Plot accuracy per convention per model with item-bootstrap bars and the paired difference per convention with its interval.
4. Measure the batch-size disagreement rate (1 versus 8) in bf16 on the 500 items and print it beside the flip table.
5. Claim that survives noise: at least one convention flips the ranking of the two checkpoints by more than the paired interval, or, if none does, the section reports the convention dependence of the margins and of the reliability diagram instead; the text is written after the grid runs.
6. Reused pieces: `d2l.generate`, `d2l.sample_logits` (1.2), `d2l.label_logprobs` (1.3) as the special case; a local 8-line bootstrap until 1.5.
**Figures:** `fig_lm_scoring_conventions` (the same item rendered under cloze, letter and generative conventions with the scored tokens marked); `fig_lm_ranking_flip` (plot: accuracy per convention per model with bars and the paired difference with its interval).
**Restate / forward:** `subsec_bits-per-byte` and `sec_mdl-coding-compression` (per-token perplexity is not comparable across tokenizers; bits per byte is, and `eq_mdl-bpc` is the conversion); `sec_seq2seq` (chrF and BLEU score n-gram overlap with a reference and nothing else); `subsec_deterministic_arithmetic` (kernel nondeterminism makes bitwise reproduction a setting, not a default); `sec_softmax` (calibration of the choice probabilities). Forward: 1.5 (the shared bootstrap and suites).
**Exercises:** 6 to 8. Load-bearing: derive the n at which the variance of the pass@k estimator halves for fixed p and k (derive); measure the effect of length normalization on HellaSwag against ARC and explain the difference by the choices' length spread (measure); implement minimum-Bayes-risk decoding over the 8-sample pool with chrF as the utility and compare with majority voting (open); check that `d2l.pass_at_k` returns 0.4 for n = 5, c = 2, k = 1 and 1.0 whenever n - c < k (check).
**Writer notes:**
- Exports with fixed contracts (`01_interfaces.md`): `d2l.score_choices(model, tokenizer, prompts, choices, norm='token', *, batch_size=8, return_components=False)` (log-softmax in fp32 whatever the model dtype; prompt and choice tokenized separately and the continuation taken as the suffix; trailing prompt whitespace moved to the choice; no BOS; an empty continuation raises); `d2l.pass_at_k(n, c, k)` vectorized over integer arrays, exact 0.0 for c = 0 and 1.0 for n - c < k; `d2l.pass_at_k_variance(n, p, k)`; `d2l.extract_answer(text, kind='gsm8k'|'boxed', strict=False)`; `d2l.bits_per_byte(model, tokenizer, texts, ctx_len=2048, stride=None, batch_size=4)` scoring every token once; `d2l.format_mc(question, options, fmt='cloze'|'letter', *, shots=())`. 8.5 composes `extract_answer` with its own `canonical_answer`; 3.4 imports `bits_per_byte` and adds `bpb_from_nll`.
- Reference implementation and tolerance: a committed fixture `lm_eval_reference_arc.json` from a pinned lm-evaluation-harness version (per-item loglikelihoods and `acc`, `acc_norm` for Qwen3-0.6B-Base on 200 items); `acc_norm`'s length definition and the continuation rule are read from that version and the fixture is regenerated if it changes.
- Scale: two checkpoints (Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B) and 500 items instead of four checkpoints and the full splits; the committed per-item scores keep the figure cells at T0.
- Sandbox: `d2l.run_python_tests` runs model-written code in a `python -I` subprocess with resource limits; the build must run that cell in a container or commit outcomes only with `RERUN=False`.
- Pitfalls to state: pass@k estimated as 1 - (1 - c/n)^k or from n = k samples; extractors crediting the last number mentioned; label-word leakage in letter-format demonstrations; scoring a reasoning model's answer option without its reasoning.
- Data: `allenai/ai2_arc` ARC-Challenge test (CC BY-SA 4.0); `openai/gsm8k` (MIT), 4-shot with the first four train problems; `Rowan/hellaswag` for the exercise (licence read from the card); `Salesforce/wikitext` test for bits per byte (not redistributed). Committed: `lm-arc-scores.parquet`, `lm-gsm8k-samples.jsonl`.
- Do not re-teach: perplexity and bits per byte (defined in `sec_language-model`), arithmetic coding (`sec_mdl-coding-compression`), chrF and BLEU (`sec_seq2seq`), seeds and determinism (`sec_repro`).
- If no flip occurs on the chosen pair, add Qwen3-1.7B-Base as a third checkpoint (one extra column, no new idea).
**Sources:**
- Papers: [Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03374) (pass@k and its unbiased estimator); [Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14782) (harness design choices and their consequences); [Leveraging Large Language Models for Multiple Choice Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.12353) (cloze against letter formats); [Holistic Evaluation of Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09110) (multi-metric reporting and calibration).
- Code and documentation: [lm-evaluation-harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) (the fixture's source; task conventions); [LightEval](https://github.com/huggingface/lighteval) (a second scorer implementation to read); [human-eval](https://github.com/openai/human-eval) (the execution protocol); [IFEval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07911) (verifiable instruction constraints, an exercise); Transformers, [perplexity guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/perplexity) (fixed-length and strided evaluation).
- Courses, tutorials and blogs: Hugging Face, [What's going on with the Open LLM Leaderboard?](https://huggingface.co/blog/open-llm-leaderboard-mmlu) (one benchmark, three implementations, three rankings); Thinking Machines, [Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference](https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/defeating-nondeterminism-in-llm-inference/) (batch-dependent kernels); [CS336](https://cs336.stanford.edu/) (evaluation lecture).

### 1.5 Evaluation Suites, Judges and Error Bars · T1
**Idea:** A benchmark has a lifecycle, and a difference counts only if it survives a paired test.
**Opening:** A model gains two points on a suite, and the reader wants to know whether the gain is real. The section asks what the suite was measuring when it was introduced and what it measures now that the field has climbed it, then builds the paired comparison that decides whether two points at this sample size is anything at all, and closes on how to write a result another lab can check.
**Teaches:**
- The benchmark lifecycle: introduced, climbed, saturated, replaced, with one dated example of each stage and a held-out tier as the cleanest design; benchmark names and dates live in `data/lm_benchmarks.json`, refreshed per edition, and prose teaches the lifecycle and the statistics.
- Development against reporting suites; `d2l.EvalSuite` with frozen task manifests, per-item results, a suite hash that changes when a dataset revision or subset changes, and `EvalResult.compare` aligned by item id.
- Paired comparison and clustered standard errors (`d2l.paired_bootstrap` with `cluster=`), the minimum detectable effect at a sample size, and multiple comparisons.
- Judges: a pairwise judge run in both orders so position bias is measured rather than assumed (`d2l.judge_pairwise`), verbosity and self-preference biases as measured rates, validation against human labels before use, and Bradley-Terry strengths from pairwise verdicts.
- The protocol `subsec_lm_reproduce_protocol` for reproducing one published number: prompts, seeds, samples, interval, detectable effect, and what was held fixed (the project scaffold's baseline step).
**Derivation:** The clustered standard error for G clusters of m items with intra-cluster correlation rho: the design effect 1 + (m - 1) rho multiplies the iid variance, so the interval widens by its square root. Smallest numeric case: G = 2 clusters of m = 2 items with rho = 1 give a design effect of 2 and an effective sample of 2, not 4. Pairing is restated, not derived: the variance of a paired difference is the iid variance times (1 - rho) between the two systems' scores on the same items.
**Notebook:**
1. Load the committed per-item scores of 1.4 for Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B on the development suite; compute unpaired and paired intervals for the difference and show the paired one is narrower by about the square root of (1 - rho).
2. On the GSM8K 8-sample pool, compute the interval treating samples as independent and with cluster resampling by problem; report the measured design effect.
3. Generate one answer per prompt from both checkpoints on 300 prompts (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.8, non-thinking); judge every pair with Qwen3.5-4B in both orders; report the position-bias distribution, the consistency rate, the verbosity slope and the win rate with a prompt-level bootstrap.
4. Validate the judge on a seeded subset of a human-labelled pairwise set and report agreement with its coverage.
5. Plot the half-width of the 95% interval against n for iid, paired and clustered designs with the measured parameters (the minimum detectable effect curve).
6. Claim that survives noise: one of the reported intervals includes zero (a difference the unpaired bars would have called real is not resolved at this n, or the reverse); position bias is nonzero and ignoring order would flip the winner of a stated fraction of pairs. Bootstrap Monte Carlo error is shown with two seeds; a second answer seed for one checkpoint pair reports whether the judged win rate moves by more than its interval.
7. Reused pieces: 1.4's scorers and sample pools; `d2l.generate`; `sec_regularized`'s Bradley-Terry likelihood fitted to judge outputs (`d2l.bradley_terry`).
**Figures:** `fig_lm_benchmark_lifecycle` (one suite's score over time through the four stages, with the data file's examples named in the caption, not the prose); `fig_lm_mde` (plot: minimum detectable effect against n for iid, paired and clustered designs).
**Restate / forward:** `subsec_mdl-paired-comparisons` (pairing removes item difficulty from the difference's variance); `ex_mdl-statistics-clustered` (clustered test sets need cluster resampling; this section builds the cluster bootstrap that exercise asked for); `sec_regularized` (Bradley-Terry: the probability that i beats j is a sigmoid of a strength difference). Forward: 8.1 (the same judge biases appear in reward models).
**Exercises:** 6 to 8. Load-bearing: derive the design effect 1 + (m - 1) rho from the variance of a cluster mean (derive); measure the judge's agreement with 200 human labels and the coverage of position-consistent verdicts, then say what agreement on easy pairs does not show (measure); apply a Bonferroni-style widening to the six-pair survival table and report what changes (check); open: write the reproduce-with-error-bars report for one published number of your choice following `subsec_lm_reproduce_protocol`.
**Writer notes:**
- Exports with fixed contracts (`01_interfaces.md`): `d2l.BootstrapResult(mean, ci, se, p_two_sided, n, n_clusters, n_boot)` (a NamedTuple; consumers read `r.mean` and `r.ci`, never a 3-tuple); `d2l.bootstrap_ci` and `d2l.paired_bootstrap(scores_a, scores_b, n_boot=10000, cluster=None, *, seed=0, alpha=0.05)` (multinomial counts and two matrix products, no Python loop over replicates; the ratio estimator for unequal clusters; a bootstrap p-value, not a permutation one, and the docstring points to `sec_mdl-statistics`' sign-flip test); `d2l.EvalTask`, `d2l.EvalSuite(tasks, name='suite', batch_size=8, *, n=None, seed=0)` with string task ids from `d2l.EVAL_TASKS` (`arc_challenge, hellaswag, mmlu, mmlu_pro, gsm8k, humaneval` and the zero-shot small-model tasks `arc_easy, piqa, sciq, winogrande`), per-item caching keyed by model id, revision and suite hash, per-item sampling seeds derived as `hash((seed, task_id, item_id))` so adding items never changes existing samples; `d2l.EvalResult.scores(task=None)`, `.compare(other)`, `.macro()`; `d2l.judge_pairwise` returning `d2l.JudgeResult(pref_a, delta, position_bias, consistent, verdict, logits)` under the additive model `delta = (l1 - l2) / 2`, `position_bias = (l1 + l2) / 2`.
- The judge is Qwen3.5-4B in bf16 (not the blueprint's Qwen3.5-9B); the lifecycle paragraph and the data file replace the blueprint's suite list; the reproduce protocol is its own `##` subsection; the second, older-family judge for the self-preference check is an exercise. Qwen3.5-4B is the same family as the answerers, so the text says so and the human-agreement table comes first.
- Data: `HuggingFaceH4/mt_bench_prompts` (Apache-2.0, first turns) plus seeded instructions from `databricks/databricks-dolly-15k` (CC BY-SA 3.0) for the 300 prompts; `lmsys/mt_bench_human_judgments` (CC BY 4.0) for validation; gated suites (GPQA, HLE) are named in the data file and not run; a moving benchmark (monthly releases) cannot be pinned by hash and the text says to record the release.
- Pitfalls to state: overlapping unpaired intervals as a test; resampling tokens or samples as if independent; a rubric that rewards length; trusting human agreement measured on easy pairs; six pairs per benchmark are multiple comparisons; "no significant difference" is not "no difference".
- Committed artifacts: `lm-eval-scores.parquet`, `lm-judge-pairs.jsonl` (logits and lengths, answer text in `lm-answers.jsonl` under the prompts' licences), `lm-judge-human.jsonl`, `data/suites/dev_v1.json` and `report_v1.json`, `JUDGE_RUBRIC_V1` as a committed string.
- Assertions: at least 30 clusters for a cluster bootstrap; a warning below 100 items; the percentile interval is not BCa (a one-line `scipy` comparison is an exercise).
- Do not re-teach: the bootstrap and percentile intervals, the sign-flip test (`sec_mdl-statistics`); the Bradley-Terry derivation (`sec_regularized`); leaderboard and saturation stories at survey level (`sec_software_ecosystem`).
- The contents of `data/lm_benchmarks.json` for this edition (one example per lifecycle stage with its date; a held-out-tier example) are approved by the owner per edition, before freeze.
**Sources:**
- Papers: [Adding Error Bars to Evals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00640) (paired differences, clustered standard errors, power: the source of the derivation); [Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685) (judge biases and agreement with humans); [Chatbot Arena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04132) (Bradley-Terry rankings from votes); [Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17926) (position bias and the two-order remedy); [LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13076) (self-preference); [The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in NLP](https://aclanthology.org/P18-1128/) (test selection).
- Code and documentation: [lm-evaluation-harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) (suites and standard errors); [LightEval](https://github.com/huggingface/lighteval); [AlpacaEval](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/alpaca_eval) (judges and length control).
- Courses, tutorials and blogs: Hamel Husain, [Your AI Product Needs Evals](https://hamel.dev/blog/posts/evals/); the [NeurIPS 2024](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/tutorial/99524) and [ICML 2024](https://icml.cc/virtual/2024/tutorial/35227) evaluation tutorials; [CMU 11-711](https://cmu-l3.github.io/anlp-spring2026) (experimental design lecture, the reproduction assignment); [CS336](https://cs336.stanford.edu/) (evaluation lecture).

### 1.6 Interpretability · T1
**Idea:** Claims about what a model computes are tested by intervening on activations, not by reading them.
**Opening:** The reader asks Qwen3-0.6B where the Eiffel Tower stands and watches the answer's rank rise through the layers under the logit lens. Reading the residual stream suggests where the fact is retrieved; only overwriting it says whether that is where. The section builds the interventions and closes on what pushing a feature costs the model elsewhere.
**Teaches:**
- The residual stream read by the logit lens and the tuned lens (`d2l.logit_lens`, `d2l.TunedLens`); linear probes with a control task, so selectivity separates what a representation encodes from what the probe learns.
- Activation patching between a clean and a corrupted prompt as a causal effect per layer and position (`d2l.intervene`); attribution patching as its first-order estimate, with the gradient cached by the same hooks.
- Sparse autoencoders as dictionary learning on the residual stream: the objective, bounded decoder norms, the top-k variant; a small SAE trained in the notebook (`d2l.TopKSAE`, `d2l.train_sae`) measured against a released Qwen-Scope SAE by L0, fraction of variance unexplained and loss recovered (`d2l.sae_metrics`).
- One steering vector with its perplexity cost beside the behaviour change; chain-of-thought monitorability in one paragraph as the bridge to reasoning traces.
- Gemma Scope 2 transcoders and an attribution graph as one exercise (the only place a third family appears, and only there).
**Derivation:** Patching as a causal effect: the metric difference when one site's activation is replaced by its value under the corrupted prompt, summed over sites to recover the total effect; its first-order form, the inner product of the activation difference with the metric's gradient at that site, and when the linearization fails. The SAE objective: reconstruction plus an L1 penalty on codes with decoder columns constrained to unit norm (otherwise the penalty is defeated by scaling), and top-k as the L0-constrained alternative. Smallest numeric case: a two-site patch where the effects do not add, computed by hand.
**Notebook:**
1. Track the rank of the correct answer across layers on 40 committed recall prompts with the logit lens and with a tuned lens trained on cached activations (or loaded from the committed translators).
2. Fit a part-of-speech probe on one layer with a control task of random tags per word type and report accuracy and selectivity.
3. Patch `resid_post` and `attn_out` at every layer and position from the corrupted to the clean run and map the effect; then compute attribution patching from one backward pass and plot its agreement with the patched map.
4. Train a top-k SAE on one layer's residual stream of Qwen3-1.7B-Base over a few million cached tokens and compare its reconstruction and loss recovered with the released Qwen-Scope SAE for the same layer; label three features by top examples and call the labels hypotheses.
5. Add one steering direction (an SAE feature chosen by contrast and a difference-of-means vector) at a grid of strengths and plot the behaviour change against the perplexity cost on held-out English text, with a random direction of the same norm as the floor.
6. Claim that survives noise: a few (layer, position) cells carry most of the patching effect for the recall behaviour (a cluster bootstrap over prompts gives the interval); attribution patching agrees with patching in rank order outside the near-zero cells; the random direction yields no behaviour change below the cost cap, and both informed directions do, with the cheaper one stated only if the frontier areas' bootstrap intervals separate.
7. Reused pieces: `d2l.load_qwen3` and the module names of 1.2, `d2l.generate`, 1.4's cross-entropy for the cost, 1.5's `d2l.bootstrap_ci(cluster=)`.
**Figures:** `fig_lm_patching` (clean and corrupted prompts, the sites, and the patching map as a heat map); `fig_lm_lens_rank` (plot: rank of the correct answer by layer under both lenses); `fig_lm_sae_frontier` (plot: the steering frontier, behaviour change against perplexity cost, for the three directions).
**Restate / forward:** `sec_what-attention-computes` (induction heads were located by ablation; `tab_induction-evidence` orders behavioural, correlational and interventional evidence, and this section climbs it); `sec_mdl-svd-low-rank` (a linear probe is a rank-one read-out and the difference-of-means vector is its simplest case); `eq_stream-update` (every block adds to a shared stream the lens reads). Forward: Chapter 9 (monitoring reasoning traces).
**Exercises:** 6 to 8. Load-bearing: derive attribution patching from the first-order expansion and bound its error by the second derivative along the patch (derive); measure the steering frontier of a second feature and of the difference-of-means direction at matched perplexity cost (measure); load a Gemma Scope 2 transcoder for one Gemma layer, build a one-step attribution graph for one prompt, and compare with the SAE view (open); check that the logit lens applied to the last layer reproduces the model's logits exactly (check).
**Writer notes:**
- Exports: `d2l.intervene(model, sites, *, record=(), record_grad=False)` as a context manager over `d2l.GPT` with site kinds `resid_post, resid_mid, attn_out, mlp_out, head_z`; `d2l.logit_lens(model, hidden, layer=None)` (applies the final norm and the tied head, fp32); `d2l.TunedLens(d_model, num_layers)` with translators initialized at zero so training starts at the logit lens; `d2l.TopKSAE(d_model, d_sae, k)` with the layout and names of Qwen-Scope's files (`W_enc (d_sae, d_model)`, `b_enc`, `W_dec (d_model, d_sae)`, `b_dec`), `normalize_decoder_()`; `d2l.load_qwen_scope_sae(repo_id, layer, revision=None, ...)` loading one `layer{n}.sae.pt` with `weights_only=True`; `d2l.sae_metrics` excluding position 0 and norm outliers (the first-token sinks the Qwen-Scope report filtered).
- Models: patching, lenses and the probe run on the book's Qwen3-0.6B (28 layers, d = 1024); the SAE cells run on Qwen3-1.7B-Base through the same `d2l.load_qwen3`, because Qwen-Scope releases SAEs for Qwen3-1.7B-Base, Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen3.5-2B-Base, not for 0.6B. One released layer is 537 MB in fp32; a layer sweep is optional. The `SMALL=True` path uses Qwen3-0.6B with its own notebook-trained SAE and no download.
- Licence: the Qwen-Scope card is tagged `license: other` with a use-restriction "Caution" paragraph while its LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 text; the notebook takes the stricter reading: run-time download only, no committed or redistributed SAE weights, the Caution quoted verbatim from the downloaded README before first use. If the editor judges the restriction incompatible with the book's licence, the released SAE becomes a pointer and the frontier uses the notebook's own SAE feature.
- Released-SAE convention: whether the encoder subtracts `b_dec` before `W_enc` is not stated on the card; decide by reconstruction, print both, and stop using the release if neither reconstructs (the instrument check fails loudly).
- Qwen-Scope is the notebook's suite; Gemma Scope 2 transcoders and the attribution graph are one exercise (no Gemma 3 run in the notebook); a monitorability paragraph is included; the five cells beyond patching (two lenses, probe, SAE, steering) are one cell each and patching is the section's experiment.
- Patching data: 40 committed (clean, corrupted, correct, distractor) prompt pairs of equal token length built from a landmark-and-city list; pairs where the clean top-1 is wrong are discarded and counted. Probe data: Universal Dependencies English EWT (CC BY-SA 4.0, pinned by commit), last sub-token per word. Contrast and cost data: FineWeb-Edu English (ODC-By) and Chinese Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0) documents at run time.
- Pitfalls to state: a probe's accuracy is not the model's use of the property; early logit-lens outputs are partly a scaling artifact; patching a corrupted prompt that differs in more than one variable; applying an SAE trained on one checkpoint to another is an assumption checked by reconstruction; steering strength is not comparable across directions unless normalized; `.pt` files load with `weights_only=True` only.
- Hooks across versions: Transformers decoder-layer outputs changed between tensor and tuple; the oracle cell handles both and asserts the last-layer relation to the final-norm output; if TransformerLens lacks Qwen3 support at the pinned version, the oracle is Transformers with hooks.
- Committed artifacts: tuned-lens translators (`lm-tuned-lens-qwen3-0.6b`, about 57 MB in fp16), probe weights, the notebook's small SAEs (`lm-sae-r1-l14`, `lm-sae-q17b-l14`, fp16), patching effect tables, steering results as CSV; none of the released SAE.
- Read the exact Gemma Scope 2 transcoder repository and layer for the exercise from the Gemma Scope page at authoring. Run-time use of Qwen-Scope is approved (academic use) under the Caution terms above.
**Sources:**

### 1.7 Models behind an API · T0
**Idea:** A hosted model is a service with a protocol, a price and limits that the client can measure, and what it cannot return is why the rest of the part works with open weights.
**Opening:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 763 billion parameters, more than one A100 node holds even at four bits, yet it answers a GSM8K problem in about a second for a printed fraction of a cent. The section treats the client as a measuring instrument (latency, throughput under concurrency, cost, reproducibility) and closes on what survives of the chapter's toolkit when the weights are someone else's.
**Teaches:**
- The chat-completions protocol: messages, sampling fields that map onto `sec_decoding`, streaming, `usage` as the ground truth for tokens and cost, `system_fingerprint` and served model id; a field probe matrix across a router, a local server and a closed provider.
- `d2l.ChatAPI`: a request-hash replay cache (`replay`, `record`, `live`), bounded concurrency with full-jitter backoff honouring `Retry-After`, a cost cap, a manifest; the SDK's own retries turned off so 429s are counted.
- Model ids drift (aliases re-pointed, providers re-quantize, `:fastest` switches providers between calls; one set of open weights is served by dozens of providers at FP4, FP8 or MXFP4, each with its own supported fields); temperature 0 with a seed is not determinism; what an API withholds: prompt log-probabilities, hidden states, weights, the sampler.
- Reasoning effort as a request field: it moves reasoning tokens (inside `completion_tokens`, reported in `usage`) and cost, not the protocol; accuracy against effort belongs to 9.6.
- Terms of use as an engineering input: which outputs may be committed, and the check 3.5, 7.3 and 9.1 run before an API model generates training data.
- The same client against `transformers serve` for a local model, so hosted and local are measured with identical prompts and extractor.
**Derivation:** Little's law for a closed loop with c in-flight requests and service time W0 at light load: throughput X = min(c / W0, Xmax), with the knee at c* = Xmax W0, and X W = c at every level; the expected sleep of full-jitter backoff after attempt a, half of min(cap, base 2^a). Smallest numeric case: W0 = 2 s and Xmax = 8 requests per second give the knee at 16 in-flight requests; the expected total sleep over six attempts with base 1 s and cap 60 s, summed by hand.
**Notebook:**
1. Probe the field matrix on three endpoints (`/v1/models`, `logprobs`, `seed`, `response_format`, thinking controls) and print it; snapshot the router listing with prices and date.
2. Experiment 1: 100 GSM8K problems (1.4's seeded ids, 4-shot through `d2l.fewshot_prompt(template='chat_multi')`) on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 through the router (one pinned provider), on Qwen3.8-27B, and on Qwen3.5-4B behind `transformers serve`; accuracy with intervals, the paired difference, latency p50 and p90, cost from `usage` reconciled with the billing page when live; the flagship run twice (replica 0 and 1) as the noise floor.
3. Experiment 2: the three longest problems, 20 replicas each at temperature 0 and a fixed seed, hosted, local alone, local under 8 background requests; count distinct completions and the first character of divergence.
4. Experiment 3: streaming on the flagship at concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 requests per level, with two shuffled passes (320 requests); throughput, time to first token, 429 counts; fit min(c / W0, Xmax).
5. One cell: the flagship at three effort settings on five committed prompts, reporting reasoning tokens, completion tokens and wall-clock (an anecdote, labelled as such).
6. Claim that survives noise: X W = c within a few percent at every level, and a knee is claimed only if both passes show it; a model gap at n = 100 smaller than the replica disagreement is called unresolved with 1.5's minimum detectable effect stated; identical outputs on 60 replicas do not show determinism, and the text says so.
7. Reused pieces: 1.3's prompt builder, 1.4's extractor and problem ids, 1.5's `paired_bootstrap` and `bootstrap_ci`; a recording makes live calls under `COST_CAP_USD = 5` (about 750 calls, estimated under $2; see "Paid API calls"), and every build replays the committed caches at T0.
**Figures:** `fig_lm_api_concurrency` (plot: throughput and time to first token against concurrency, the fitted closed-loop curve, 429 counts as labels); `fig_lm_api_lost` (what the open-weights toolkit of 1.2 to 1.6 can see and what each endpoint type returns, as a table-like figure).
**Restate / forward:** `sec_decoding` (request fields are the sampler's parameters: temperature, top-p, stop); `sec_repro` (a seed promises reproducibility only for a sampler you own). Forward: 10.1 (the `tools` field).
**Exercises:** 5 to 7. Load-bearing: derive W(c) beyond the knee from X W = c and the saturated throughput (derive); measure prompt-cache hits on a shared 2,000-token prefix through `usage.cached_tokens` and the cost difference (measure); check that the request hash excludes `stream` and the API key and includes `replica`, by constructing colliding and non-colliding requests (check); open: run Experiment 1 through an FP4 and an FP8 provider of the same weights and test whether the accuracy difference exceeds the replica disagreement, or run 1.5's judge through the router on 100 pairs and compare its position bias with the local judge's.
**Writer notes:**
- Exports (`01_interfaces.md`): `d2l.ChatAPI(base_url, model, api_key=None, *, cache=None, mode='replay', price=None, cost_cap_usd=None, timeout=120.0, max_retries=6, default_params=None, http_client=None)` with `.chat(messages, *, replica=0, stream=False, **params) -> d2l.ChatResult`, `async .achat`, `.models()`, `.spent_usd`, `.manifest()`; `mode='replay'` raises `d2l.ReplayMiss` on a miss so a build can never reach the network; a live call past the cap raises `d2l.CostCapExceeded`; `d2l.chat_batch(api, requests, *, concurrency=8)` returns results in input order with failures as exceptions; `d2l.backoff_delay(attempt, base=1.0, cap=60.0, rng=None, retry_after=None)`; `d2l.PricePoint(input, output, cached_input=None, per=1_000_000)` and `d2l.api_cost(usage, price)`; `d2l.price_from_listing`. The request hash is the sha256 of canonical JSON over host, model, messages, sampling and format params and `replica`; it excludes `stream`, timeouts, headers and keys. The API key is never read from a file and never enters the hash, cache or logs.
- Wrap `openai.OpenAI` with `max_retries=0` (the SDK retries twice by default and would hide 429s from the counters); retry only connection errors, timeouts and 408, 429, 5xx; raise at once on 400, 401, 403, 404, 422.
- The flagship is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (MIT, open weights, 763B parameters in a sparse mixture of experts), always by its dated snapshot id, never the re-pointable alias `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the second hosted arm is Qwen3.8-27B (Apache-2.0, open weights a T2 pair can serve, the larger sibling of the local arm's family); the local arm is Qwen3.5-4B behind `transformers serve` (not Qwen3.5-9B, as the blueprint has it). Pin one provider per model through the router's provider preferences with fallbacks off, choosing one that exposes `logprobs`, `seed` and `structured_outputs` (on 2026-11-06 Morph, Nebius and Novita did for the flagship; DeepSeek's own route lacked `seed` and doubles its price in two weekday windows, 01:00 to 04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC); record the served model id and provider with every response; `:fastest` switches providers between calls. Fallback if the snapshot leaves the router: the undated alias with the served id recorded, else Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B at about ten times the price. The release ships no chat template, only a Python prompt encoder, so the hosted arm also withholds how the prompt is encoded.
- `transformers serve` is documented as experimental and rejects `logprobs`, `n`, `response_format`; the probe matrix is the evidence; fallback for the local arm is vLLM in its own environment. The `d2l.ChatAPI` is a measurement and replay client; 13.1's load-testing client is a different object and neither imports the other.
- Terms and costs: live runs go through OpenRouter (or a similar aggregator; the Hugging Face router needs a Hub token with the Inference Providers permission) with the token held outside the repository and a fixed per-build budget set as a notebook constant (the cost cap); prices in the listing carry no stated unit, so reconcile with the billing page and use it when they disagree; outputs of the MIT and Apache-2.0 models are committed with attribution, a closed provider's outputs never.
- Pitfalls to state: timing whole responses and calling it latency; counting streamed chunks as tokens; a `max_tokens` that hidden reasoning consumes (reasoning tokens are inside completion tokens unless the provider says otherwise, asserted from `usage`); comparing local and hosted under different prompts, thinking modes or extractors.
- Committed artifacts: `lm-api-gsm8k-v1`, `lm-api-determinism-v1`, `lm-api-sweep-v1`, `lm-api-judge-v1`, `lm-api-effort-v1` (JSONL caches), `lm-api-listing-v1` (the `/v1/models` rows with date), `manifest.json` per cache, `lm-api-fields.csv`.
- Keep the section short (about 2,000 words); the derivation and three experiments are each one `##` subsection.
- Confirm at authoring the snapshot id, its licence file and the pinned providers' supported fields, and re-snapshot the listing with prices and date.
**Sources:**
- Papers: [Model Equality Testing: Which Model Is This API Serving?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20247) (statistical tests that an endpoint serves the model it claims); [Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715) (substitution and quantization at providers).
- Code and documentation: Hugging Face, [Inference Providers](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index) (the router, provider policies and the `model:provider` suffix), its [chat-completion specification](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/tasks/chat-completion) and [pricing and billing](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/pricing); [openai-python](https://github.com/openai/openai-python) (clients, `usage` types, default retries); Transformers, [Serving](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/serving) (`transformers serve`, its endpoints and limits); vLLM, [OpenAI-compatible server](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/serving/online_serving/) (the local fallback); [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 model card](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) (the flagship: licence, recommended sampling, the prompt encoder); [Qwen3.8 README](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.8) (the second arm's controls); OpenRouter, [provider selection](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection) (pinning a provider with fallbacks off) and [reasoning tokens](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/reasoning-tokens) (the `reasoning` field; reasoning tokens count against the output limit); [RFC 6585](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6585) (HTTP 429).
- Courses, tutorials and blogs: AWS Architecture Blog, [Exponential Backoff and Jitter](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/) (the schedules behind `backoff_delay`); Thinking Machines, [Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference](https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/defeating-nondeterminism-in-llm-inference/) (why temperature 0 is not deterministic); [lm-evaluation-harness API guide](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/blob/main/docs/API_guide.md) (evaluating through chat completions).
## Chapter 2 Encoders, Embeddings and Retrieval

**Label:** `chap_lm_encoders`. Five sections plus one Further Reading notebook, T1 throughout (2.1 also runs on CPU). The chapter covers the pretrained encoders and embedding models that still do the work in search, filtering, tagging and retrieval, and the retrieval systems built on them; it replaces the two retiring NLP chapters.
**Hook:** The reader has a decoder that answers questions but no way to find, among a million passages, the one that holds the answer, and no cheap way to label ten thousand sentences an hour.
**Route:** What statistic does a word vector factorize (2.1)? What does a masked-token encoder give per token, and when does fine-tuning it beat prompting a decoder (2.2)? Why do pooled encoder states retrieve poorly until contrastive training spreads them on the sphere (2.3)? What does an index trade for speed, and what floor must a dense index beat (2.4)? Where does a retrieval-augmented system fail, and how is the failing stage found (2.5)?
**Out of scope:** Encoder pretraining at scale (`sec_transformer` builds and trains the bidirectional encoder; 2.2 starts from a released checkpoint), agent loops that call retrieval as a tool (`chap_lm_agents`), multimodal retrieval (the Image Models part), learned sparse retrieval and late interaction (the Further Reading notebook).
**Writer notes:**
- Running models (Table 5): ModernBERT-base (encoder), Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (embedder), Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B (reranker), Qwen3-1.7B (few-shot comparison in 2.2), Qwen3-4B (generator in 2.5), Qwen3.5-4B in bf16 (judge; not the blueprint's Qwen3.5-9B).
